clue.text: Pilot flying in a war round centre of Colombia

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters sit around the Colombian centre
flying suggests letters sent loose and rearranged in a new order
centre of picks the two middle letters of the eight-letter country name

explanation.surface: An aviator serving in a war flies a mission over the middle of Colombia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges IN A WAR into AIRWAN; 'round' puts it around OM, the middle two letters of Colombia, from 'centre of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who flies an aircraft is a pilot, so the general term defines her.

clue.text: Initially some people accept many unwelcome emails

indicators.note: Initially tells the solver to take the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Some people put up with lots of junk messages in their inbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk messages sent in bulk without being asked for are known by this name, after a tinned meat.

clue.text: Rubbish rhymes?

parts.note: rubbish means nonsense talk, and the word for it is made of two halves that rhyme with each other

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the wordplay: the nonsense word itself is a rhyming pair, 'clap' and 'trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty, showy talk meant to win applause is nonsense, the sense of rubbish here.

clue.text: College determined to, dismissing head

indicators.note: dismissing head means the first letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to be set on doing something is to be determined to do it

explanation.surface: A college resolved to sack its headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing head' takes S off SET ON. 'head' looks like the school's headteacher, but it is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English boarding school near Windsor.

clue.text: Girl's wearing ruby and wedding band as a distraction

indicators.note: wearing means the girl's pronoun is inside the jewellery words that she wears

parts.note: ruby is a deep shade of red
a wedding band is a ring
the girl's things are hers, giving the pronoun her

explanation.surface: A bride shows off a ruby and a wedding band, drawing everyone's eye away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' is the container signal: the girl has the jewellery on, so the jewellery words go around her pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue planted to draw attention elsewhere is an idiomatic name for a diversion.

clue.text: A woman from America in a different country

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: An American woman finds herself overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overseas means being in a foreign land, away from home.

clue.text: Against keeping paintings in box

indicators.note: keeping means the word for against holds the art inside it

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: Someone objects to storing pictures in a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard container is a box, such as one holding milk or eggs.

clue.text: Terribly involved ultimately, absorb from cover to cover

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word involved

parts.note: to absorb a book from cover to cover is to read it fully

explanation.surface: A reader gets terribly involved and devours a book from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives D, the last letter of 'involved'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean awfully or very badly, so one swaps for the other.

clue.text: 'Goodbye', army repeated

indicators.note: repeated says the army abbreviation is written twice

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A soldier's farewell, said over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is the British army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual British farewell, informal for bye-bye.

clue.text: Discharge people for sports day event

parts.note: to sack someone is to discharge them from a job
a race is a people sharing descent

explanation.surface: A school fires staff ahead of its sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: A sports day is a British school athletics day; in this race children hop along inside sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping along in a bag is a classic novelty contest at school athletics days.

clue.text: Recalled part of Primal Scream hit

indicators.note: Recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A song by the band Primal Scream is remembered as a big chart success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' gives MALS from 'priMAL Scream'; 'Recalled' turns it round. 'hit' looks like a chart song but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike forcefully is to hit, as in slamming a door or a ball.

clue.text: Tape collection finally put inside holder

indicators.note: inside says the collection plus final letter go within the holder

parts.note: a case is something that holds things
a set is a collection

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word put

explanation.surface: Someone gathers up tape and stores it in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T, the last letter of 'put'; 'inside' puts SETT within CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a cartridge of magnetic tape for audio or video.

clue.text: Very clever structure

definitions.meaning: a curved span such as one over a doorway or bridge

explanation.surface: A building of great ingenuity.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is cunning or knowing; the other is a curved supporting span in building.

clue.text: Way speaker's travelled

indicators.note: speaker's says the word is as heard when spoken

parts.note: rode means travelled, on a horse or a bike

explanation.surface: How a speaker got to the venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker's' signals that RODE is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route or path, a way to get somewhere.

clue.text: Likely location of suits?

definitions.meaning: hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades appear printed on playing cards

explanation.surface: Where a tailor's jackets are probably found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' looks like clothing but means the four card suits.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means probable, from fortune-telling with cards; literally the suits are printed on playing cards.

clue.text: Beset by pain, old man is brave

indicators.note: Beset by means the father figure is surrounded by the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain
old man is informal for father, giving pa

explanation.surface: An elderly man in agony is being courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective, but here it is a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a warrior of a Native American people, and the Apache are one such people.

clue.text: Paddy's welcoming group of three country lovers

indicators.note: welcoming means the trio is taken inside Paddy's name

parts.note: Pat is a short form of Patrick, as is Paddy, so Paddy's gives Pat's, written as pats
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: An Irishman hosts a trio of folk who love the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: People devoted to their homeland, loving their nation, are patriots.

clue.text: Fellow, getting old, able to cope

parts.note: a fellow is a man
getting old is ageing, spelt here aging

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman is still getting by.
explanation.definitionFit: To be managing is to be getting by, coping with circumstances.

clue.text: Unusually large skate in these expanses of water

indicators.note: Unusually says the letters of the two words appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A big fish is found out of place in these North American lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skate' is a flat fish, and Lakes Superior, Michigan and others are freshwater, which is why its presence is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: The five huge connected freshwater bodies on the US–Canada border are collectively known by this name.

clue.text: Instructions from staff on nights out

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the staff word on top of the nights out

parts.note: to man something is to staff it
dates are romantic nights out

explanation.surface: An employer issues orders to workers about evenings off.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandates are official orders or authorisations to act.

clue.text: Drink making teenager sozzled

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the word's letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink that gets a youngster tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' suggests alcohol, but the answer is anything but.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfermented tea popular in East Asia is a beverage, a drink.

clue.text: Country where man meets an Australian leader

parts.note: guy is informal for a man

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of Australian

explanation.surface: A man encounters an Aussie leader on a foreign trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a nation on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Agreement giving power to do something

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
to act is to do something

explanation.surface: A deal grants the authority to take action.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement or treaty.

clue.text: His Excellency receives queen in this place

indicators.note: receives means the ambassador's title takes the queen inside it

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An ambassador welcomes the monarch at this venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at this spot, the location of the speaker.
